Mr. Puneet Singh Bindra, Adv.(Intervenor) UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following O R D E R SLP (CIVIL) Diary No(s).
28684/2021 Heard the learned ASG appearing for the petitioners, the learned counsel appearing for the land-owners and the learned counsel appearing for the Delhi Development Authority1
In this petition, there is a delay of 2241 days.
This petition is sought to be filed on the basis of a decision of the Constitution Bench in the case of Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and ors.2

entities.text: Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and ors.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present petition is filed about 20 months after the date on which the decision of the Constitution Bench was pronounced.
We are conscious of the fact that when it comes to condonation of delay, the Courts have to adopt justice oriented and liberal approach.

Apart from the observations made in the earlier orders about the manner in which Delhi Government and the DDA are filing petitions challenging decisions of the Delhi High Court invoking Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 has 1DDA 2 (2020) 8 scc 129 been noted in the orders passed by this Court and especially the order passed on 16.05.2023.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: By the order dated 13.04.2023, this Court recorded two facts; one is that though, a long counter affidavit running into 17 pages was filed by the DDA, the fact that the earlier petition filed by the DDA was dismissed, was suppressed.
Secondly, the DDA has not recorded in the said affidavit that the acquired land has been utilized for a public purpose.
The issue of suppression of fact has been addressed by this Court.
The Commissioner of the DDA appeared through video conferencing and tendered apology.

In the latest affidavit filed by the DDA, in paragraph 13, it is merely stated by the DDA that the possession of the acquired land has been handed over way back on 2 nd August, 2006 to the beneficiary department.
However, notwithstanding the opportunities granted repeatedly by this Court, the DDA has not come out in the case that the land has been used for the public purpose for which it was acquired.
Only on this Court, we are not inclined to condone the long delay of 2241 days.
Therefore, as far as merits of the SLP are concerned, we are concluding the issue.

sentences.text: However, in the order of this Court dated 16.05.2023, it was observed that there is a complete lack of coordination between the Delhi Government and the DDA when it comes to filing Special Leave Petitions based on the decision of the Constitution Bench in the case of Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and ors.3

entities.text: Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal and ors.3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pursuant to the said observation, the learned ASG and the learned counsel appearing for the State Government had stated that both the authorities will work out standard operating procedure for taking appropriate decisions regarding filing of the Special Leave Petitions based on the decision of the Constitution Bench.
Alongwith the affidavit of the DDA dated 23.07.2023, minutes of the meeting dated 24.07.2023 have been placed on record.
The Officials of the DDA and the Delhi Government attended the meeting.
A perusal of paragraph 5 of the minutes shows that the decisions arrived at in the meeting take both the authorities no where.
What we expected was that a standard operating procedure will be evolved regarding filing of the petitions based on the decision of the Constitution Bench in the case of Indore Development Authority.
We have come across the cases whereby suppressing the fact that earlier SLPs were dismissed, fresh SLPs have been filed.
We have also noticed only in selected cases, the Delhi Government and the DDA are filing SLPs based on the decision of the Constitution Bench.
We hold that the decision taken in the meeting dated 24.07.2023 is not in terms of what was assured before this Court.
We, therefore, direct the Delhi Government and the DDA to come out with proper standard operating procedure.
The standard operating procedure must involve a decision making process by which the 3 (2020) 8 scc 129 competent authorities will examine whether a case deserves to be taken to this Court or not.
The authorities cannot pick and choose when it comes to filing SLPs in this Court.
The decision must be based on a rational policy.
We direct both the Delhi Government and the DDA to come out with proper standard operating procedure.
To enable them to do so and only for that purpose, we direct that petition shall be listed on 26.09.2023 on the top of the Board.
Diary No(s).
29471/2021 Even as of today, the petitioners have not complied with the order dated 10.02.2023.
Faced with this difficulty, learned ASG seeks permission to withdraw the SLP with liberty to file a fresh petition.
While we grant the liberty, we make it clear that even in this SLP, the delay has not been condoned and the notice has been issued on condonation of delay application.
Accordingly, we dispose of the SLP with liberty to file a fresh SLP.
We make it clear that the grant of liberty shall not be construed to mean that this Court has accepted the explanation offered for the condonation of delay.
The SLP is disposed of as withdrawn.
(INDU MARWAH) (AVGV RAMU)
